messages.author: 80defc9c4046a73b
messages.subject: Re: app dependencies on other packages
parts:
Well, a shiny app is just a collection of R scripts, therefore you could do something like...

if(!require(FOO)) {install.packages("FOO",repos="http://cran.us.r-project.org");require(FOO);}

The only problem is that if a user runs your app via runUrl() or something without knowing what they're getting into, you'll be installing software on their local machine without their explicit permission. You could put a button into your app that installs the missing packages if the user signals agreement by clicking it. Alternatively, you could have the app output a message like... "This app needs the following packages: FOO, BAR, BAZ in order to function. To get the normal app functionality instead of this message, please install these packages or ask the administrator of this server to do so."

parts: I don't understand why you need NAMESPACE and DESCRIPTION actually. You can use require() to test whether a package is installed or rownames(installed.packages()) to get the list of installed packages.

messages.subject: Re: app dependencies on other packages
parts:
In that case, how about creating a custom, almost empty package and specifying the NAMESPACE and DESCRIPTION as desired? Put that package on gitorious or one of the proprietary repository sites.

Then, only one package (in this example named FOO) needs to be checked and if missing, installed explicitly:

library(devtools);
if(!require(FOO)) {install_gitorious(FOO); require(FOO)}

Warning: I have not tried this myself. I can't think of a reason this shouldn't work, but that doesn't mean there isn't one.
